To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a humanoid robot with a distributed, parallel, cognitive control architecture can learn and execute a wide variety of tasks in a human centered environment, that the robot can be teleoperated by a human, and that it can diagnose faults and recover from them.

a parallel distributed cognitive control system for a humanoid robot can be implemented using off-the-shelf components, can be applied to physically heterogeneous robots, and can provide a framework for the development of intelligent robots that interact with people.
the parallel distributed cognitive architecture is a promising approach to the design of a control system for a humanoid robot.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a cognitive control system for a physically heterogeneous robot.
the design of a control system that is general and flexible enough to support a broad range of intelligent behaviors, including motion learning, fault diagnosis, and human interaction.
the development of a cognitive control system for humanoid robots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ISAC control system is an example of a cognitive control system that has been developed for a humanoid robot, yet is applicable to a wide range of robotic applications, from industrial to service robots, to multi-robot systems, and even to human-robot teams.
ISAC’s control system is a work in progress.

the ISAC control system has evolved from the original vision of an anthropomorphic robot with human-like capabilities to a general purpose control system for a physically heterogeneous robot that can be used to control a single robot or multiple robots in a human centered environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ISAC system has evolved from a programmer’s control system toward a cognitive system capable of learning from its environment and from human interactions.
a parallel distributed cognitive control system for a humanoid robot can provide a foundation for a wide range of applications.
the ISAC system has been successful in achieving its design goals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a robot can be made to be intelligent by giving it a cognitive control system that is capable of learning and interacting with humans.
a parallel distributed control architecture, based on the principles of cognitive robotics, can be used to develop intelligent behavior for a physically complex robot.
a cognitive control system for a humanoid robot must be based on a parallel, distributed architecture that is capable of supporting a range of cognitive functions.
